reader.requirement: At --std 85 data-name-2 and data-name-3 of a RENAMES entry may each be qualified (IN or OF, by one or more higher-level data-names and, outermost, by the file-name of the FD whose record holds them), the qualification selects the item, and because §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 requires qualification of every explicitly referenced non-unique name (redefinition alone excepted) an unqualified or insufficiently qualified operand that is not unique in the program must be refused.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002: from 2002 the record's subtree is the candidate set (superordinate groups as implicit qualifiers, §2002 F.2 item 67); at 1985 RegionClauseCandidates counts the whole scope's candidates, so a name also declared in another record must be explicitly qualified, then IsWithinRegion confines the survivor to the record

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 1985 an unqualified operand whose name is also declared in another record is ambiguous (COBOL1639); at 2023 the record supplies implicit qualifiers and the same entry compiles (p5_unq_cross prints R=ABCDEF at --std 2023)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness qualifies by data-names within one record; qualification by a file-name, the cross-record ambiguity the 1985 arm decides, a wrong or misordered qualifier and an insufficiently qualified data-name-3 are not exercised

reader.notes: Both operands carry their IN/OF qualifiers into the resolve pass, which matches the chain inner to outer with gaps and a file-name outermost. At 85 the candidates are scope-wide (no 2002 implicit qualification), which is what the 1985 qualification rule requires; a misqualified operand that resolves outside the record is refused by SR4's message rather than a qualification message, which is a wording matter.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: c4_fd_unq (two FDs, identical record layouts, 'RENAMES FA THRU FB' unqualified after F2's record) refused COBOL1639 for both operands (the 1985 scope-wide arm, IV.4.3.8.1); c4_insuff ('A OF S THRU D' where S.A exists in G1 and G2) refused COBOL1639, c4_suff ('A OF S OF G2 THRU D') printed R=ABCD; c4_link_amb (A in a Working-Storage record and in the Linkage record the entry follows) refused COBOL1639; c4_outer_scope (A in the containing program's GLOBAL record, RENAMES A in the contained program's own record) printed R=ABCD, correct since the contained program's own A is the unique local resource (X.4 scope conventions); c4_sdq (qualification by an SD file-name, 'K IN SF THRU V OF SREC OF SF', a same-layout WS group present) printed SR1=AAYY / SR1=BBXX through SORT; c4_index (index-name A and data-name A) refused COBOL2692, correct at 1985 (index-names are their own disjoint set, IV.4.2.2.1.1). Cite: OK §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR5; OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 (SR3) 'Identical user-defined names may appear in a source program'; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 '4. condition-names, data-names, and record-names'; OK §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 'can belong to one and only one of these disjoint sets'. SIBLING DEFECT FOUND (another rule, not this one's path): c4_cond_nor (88 A under G1's X, 05 A under G2, references 'A OF X' and 'A OF G2', no RENAMES) is refused COBOL2692 'names two types of user-defined word (condition-name and data-name)' at --std 85, though §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1 puts condition-names, data-names and record-names in ONE disjoint set; c4_cond_q (the same with '66 R RENAMES A OF G2 THRU D') is refused the same way. Harm rejects-legal-source; cause (a): UserWordKind.cs#MayBeOneWord and its MayShareOneName set are the §2023:8.3.2.2 exception 3 list at every edition. At --std 2023 c4_cond_nor is refused the same way (correct there by 2023's list, a pointer only). No kb/Work note found (grep of COBOL2692, MayBeOneWord, 'condition-names, data-names'). The refusal fires at the declaration whether or not a RENAMES exists, so it does not overturn SR5; it does mean SR5's resolver has never been exercised at 85 with a condition-name homonym as a candidate.
